It merges content from multiple version lineages: '' '''v1.0.0 Framework''' (Constitutional_index.md, Constitutional_index1.md): Philosophical foundations, epistemic framework, research integration '' '''v2.0.0 Index''' (Constitutional_index2-5.md): Constitutional hierarchy, amendment process, SMW implementation '' '''v3.0.0 Index''' (Constitutional_index6.md): Streamlined structure with core principles focus '' '''v2.established''' (Constitutional_index7.md): SMW property refinements == Section I: Constitutional Documents (v2.0.0/v3.0.0 Structure) == BITwiki's constitutional framework consists of three interconnected documents: === BITwiki Charter === '''Status:''' Foundational declaration '''Scope:''' Mission, values, core commitments '''Location:''' [[BITwiki Charter]] The Charter declares our purpose. It establishes what BITwiki is—a recursive intelligence field for systems science knowledge. It articulates our core commitments: radical epistemic humility, radical skepticism, hyper-realism, nullification of non-signals, scoped recursion, ontological transparency. Read this first if you want to understand why BITwiki exists and what principles guide it. === BITwiki Constitution === '''Status:''' Structural framework '''Scope:''' Organizational structure, processes, epistemic framework '''Location:''' [[BITwiki Constitution]] The Constitution establishes the architectural framework. It defines our ontological approach—flexible types, not rigid categories. It articulates our epistemic framework—graduated markers, not numerical scores. It describes our recursive architecture and field coherence. Read this if you want to understand how BITwiki is structured and how it operates. === BITwiki Foundational Triad === '''Status:''' Conceptual foundation '''Scope:''' Core concepts and their interrelationships '''Location:''' [[BITwiki Foundational Triad]] The Triad defines the three foundational concepts: Axiology (value), Semantics (meaning), Axology (action). It explains how they interpenetrate and how they generate derivative principles. Read this if you want to understand the conceptual underpinnings of BITwiki approach. === BITwiki Evidence and Epistemics === '''Status:''' Operational protocol '''Scope:''' How we evaluate evidence and mark confidence '''Location:''' [[BITwiki Evidence and Epistemics]] This document defines how BITwiki records evidence quality, epistemic status, and confidence rationale. It establishes our approach to source evaluation and claim structure. Read this if you want to understand how we know what we claim to know. == Section II: Core Principles (v3.0.0 Enhanced) == === Radical Epistemic Humility === All knowledge is provisional. We mark confidence not to display certainty but to calibrate doubt. Every claim carries uncertainty. Every model simplifies. Every framework has boundaries. This is not modesty. It is precision. A claim with explicit uncertainty is more valuable than one with false confidence. === Radical Skepticism === We apply systematic doubt to all claims, including our own. No immunity. No authority beyond question. We doubt the instruments of our doubt. This is not cynicism. It is rigor. Beliefs strengthened through trial are stronger than those protected from test. === Hyper-Realism === We maintain fidelity to system dynamics over representational accuracy. Models are evaluated by predictive power, not pictorial fidelity. Truth is operational coherence. This is not relativism. Some models work better than others. But the criterion is performance, not correspondence to inaccessible reality. === Nullification of Non-Signals === We reject noise, fluff, filler, corporate language. Signal preservation requires noise suppression. Every word earns its place. This is not minimalism for its own sake. It is respect for attention. Readers have limited time. We do not waste it. === Ontological Transparency === We make structure explicit and machine-readable. Entity types, relationships, epistemic status—all declared, all queryable. This is not bureaucracy. It is enabling infrastructure. When structure is explicit, machines can navigate it. When machines can navigate it, humans can query in powerful ways. == Section III: Constitutional Hierarchy (v2.0.0 Detailed) == === 1. The constitution acknowledges uncertainty and mandates explicit confidence scoring. '''Implications:''' '' No claim to absolute truth '' Continuous revision '' Transparent uncertainty '' Evidence-based updates === Recursive Self-Reference === The constitution applies to itself. It can be revised through the processes it defines. '''Implications:''' '' Self-correcting '' Evolving framework '' Meta-level consistency '' Bootstrap capability === Distributed Governance === No single entity controls BITwiki. Governance emerges from collective intelligence. procedures '' Regular review cycles '' Sunset clauses '' Version tracking == Section VIII: Philosophical Foundations (v1.0.0 Framework) == === Process Over Substance === Traditional knowledge systems treat reality as made of static things—substances with fixed properties. BITwiki follows a different approach based on process philosophy. Alfred North Whitehead's Process and Reality (1929) established that reality consists not of static substances but of "actual occasions"—momentary events of becoming. Knowledge is not a picture of fixed reality but a grasping of ongoing processes. This matters for BITwiki because: '' Knowledge artifacts are events, not objects '' Understanding emerges from ongoing engagement '' Revision is not correction but continuation '''Source''': Whitehead, A.N. (1929). ''Process and Reality''. Free Press. === Knowledge as Practice === Michel Foucault's Archaeology of Knowledge (1969) analyzed how knowledge is produced through specific practices. Knowledge is not discovered but constructed through historical discursive formations. Key insight: What counts as knowledge depends on the practices that produce it. Different practices produce different knowledges. There is no neutral view from nowhere. This informs BITwiki approach: '' All knowledge is situated in specific practices '' We document the practices, not just the results '' Multiple practices can produce valid but different knowledges '''Source''': Foucault, M. (1969). ''The Archaeology of Knowledge''. Routledge. === The Mangle of Practice === Andrew Pickering's The Mangle of Practice (1995) describes scientific practice as open-ended interplay between human and material agency. Knowledge emerges from the "dance of agency"—scientists propose, materials resist, scientists accommodate. This dynamic model replaces the static "scientific method" with ongoing tuning and adjustment. Knowledge is always provisional, always subject to further negotiation. BITwiki applies this by: '' Treating knowledge as ongoing process, not fixed product '' Expecting resistance and accommodation '' Building in mechanisms for continuous tuning '''Source''': Pickering, A. (1995). ''The Mangle of Practice''. University of Chicago Press. == Section IX: Epistemic Framework (v1.0.0 Framework) == === Context-Dependent Evidence === Evidence has no fixed value. What counts as good evidence depends on context. A peer-reviewed paper may be flawed by funding bias. An informal forum post may contain crucial technical detail. Blockchain data is valuable for blockchain analysis, irrelevant for biology. This follows from the research: '' Whitehead's prehension: grasping depends on the grasper '' Foucault's episteme: what counts as evidence varies by historical period '' Stengers' cosmopolitics: different actors have different evidentiary standards '''Source''': Stengers, I. (1996-1997). ''Cosmopolitics''. University of Minnesota Press. === Signal Fidelity === Claude Shannon's "A Mathematical Theory of Communication" (1948) established information theory. The signal-to-noise ratio measures meaningful information relative to interference. BITwiki applies this conceptually: '' Not all information is equally valuable '' Noise is context-dependent (what distracts in one context may inform in another) '' Quality is measured by signal fidelity, not volume '''Source''': Shannon, C.E. (1948). "A Mathematical Theory of Communication." ''Bell System Technical Journal''. Gregory Bateson extended this: "Information is a difference that makes a difference." Not all differences matter. The key is identifying which differences produce change in the receiving system. '''Source''': Bateson, G. (1972). ''Steps to an Ecology of Mind''. Chandler Publishing. === Autopoiesis and Self-Production === Maturana and Varela's Autopoiesis and Cognition (1980) defined living systems as self-producing. A living system produces its own components and maintains its own organization. BITwiki is designed as autopoietic: '' It produces its own knowledge components '' It maintains its own organizational structure '' It adapts through structural coupling with its environment '''Source''': Maturana, H.R. & Varela, F.J. (1980). ''Autopoiesis and Cognition''. D. Reidel. == Section X: The Three Documents Framework (v1.0.0) == === Charter: Values and Mission === The Charter establishes what BITwiki values and why it exists. It draws on: '' Axiology (study of values) as primary '' Hyper-realism: acknowledging constructed nature of knowledge '' Epistemic humility: openness to revision Values determine what we seek to know. They come first in the framework. === Constitution: Operations === The Constitution defines how BITwiki runs. It implements: '' Agent-centric authorship: AI agents execute human intent '' Context-dependent evidence: no fixed hierarchies '' Continuous refinement: knowledge as ongoing process Methods follow from values. How we know depends on what we value knowing. === Foundational Triad: Structure === The Triad explains the philosophical architecture: '' Axiology (values) first '' Epistemology (knowledge methods) second '' Ontology (what exists) third Structure emerges from values and methods. What we can represent depends on how we know and what we care about. == Section XI: Key Principles in Practice (v1.0.0) == === No Truth by Consensus === Agreement does not equal truth. Many sources can agree and still be wrong. This follows from: '' Foucault's analysis of power/knowledge '' Pickering's mangle: consensus can be stabilization of network, not truth '' Shannon's information theory: redundancy enables error correction but does not guarantee accuracy === Human Intent First === All knowledge starts with human values. AI agents execute that intent. This follows from: '' Whitehead's actual occasions: experience is primary '' Bateson's ecology of mind: cognition is systemic process '' Autopoiesis: systems self-produce based on their own organization === Continuous Refinement === Nothing is final. All content is subject to revision. This follows from: '' Process philosophy: reality is becoming, not being '' The mangle: ongoing tuning and adjustment '' Information theory: updating based on new signals == Section XII: Research Integration (v1.0.0) == The constitutional framework synthesizes research from: {| class="wikitable" ! Models are evaluated by predictive power, not pictorial fidelity. Truth is operational coherence. This is not relativism. Some models work better than others. But the criterion is performance, not correspondence to inaccessible reality. === Nullification of Non-Signals === We reject noise, fluff, filler, corporate language. Signal preservation requires noise suppression. Every word earns its place. This is not minimalism for its own sake. It is respect for attention. Readers have limited time. We do not waste it. === Ontological Transparency === We make structure explicit and machine-readable. Entity types, relationships, epistemic status—all declared, all queryable. This is not bureaucracy. It is enabling infrastructure. When structure is explicit, machines can navigate it. (1929). ''Process and Reality''. Free Press. === Knowledge as Practice === Michel Foucault's Archaeology of Knowledge (1969) analyzed how knowledge is produced through specific practices. Knowledge is not discovered but constructed through historical discursive formations. Key insight: What counts as knowledge depends on the practices that produce it. Different practices produce different knowledges. There is no neutral view from nowhere. This informs BITwiki approach: '' All knowledge is situated in specific practices '' We document the practices, not just the results '' Multiple practices can produce valid but different knowledges '''Source''': Foucault, M. (1969). ''The Archaeology of Knowledge''. Knowledge emerges from the "dance of agency"—scientists propose, materials resist, scientists accommodate. This dynamic model replaces the static "scientific method" with ongoing tuning and adjustment. Knowledge is always provisional, always subject to further negotiation. (1995). ''The Mangle of Practice''. University of Chicago Press. == Section IX: Epistemic Framework (v1.0.0 Framework) == === Context-Dependent Evidence === Evidence has no fixed value. (1996-1997). ''Cosmopolitics''. University of Minnesota Press. === Signal Fidelity === Claude Shannon's "A Mathematical Theory of Communication" (1948) established information theory. The signal-to-noise ratio measures meaningful information relative to interference. BITwiki applies this conceptually: '' Not all information is equally valuable '' Noise is context-dependent (what distracts in one context may inform in another) '' Quality is measured by signal fidelity, not volume '''Source''': Shannon, C.E. (1948). "A Mathematical Theory of Communication." ''Bell System Technical Journal''. Gregory Bateson extended this: "Information is a difference that makes a difference." Not all differences matter. The key is identifying which differences produce change in the receiving system. '''Source''': Bateson, G. (1972). ''Steps to an Ecology of Mind''. Chandler Publishing. === Autopoiesis and Self-Production === Maturana and Varela's Autopoiesis and Cognition (1980) defined living systems as self-producing. A living system produces its own components and maintains its own organization. BITwiki is designed as autopoietic: '' It produces its own knowledge components '' It maintains its own organizational structure '' It adapts through structural coupling with its environment '''Source''': Maturana, H.R. & Varela, F.J. (1980). ''Autopoiesis and Cognition''. D. Reidel. == Section X: The Three Documents Framework (v1.0.0) == === Charter: Values and Mission === The Charter establishes what BITwiki values and why it exists. What we can represent depends on how we know and what we care about. == Section XI: Key Principles in Practice (v1.0.0) == === No Truth by Consensus === Agreement does not equal truth. treat reality as made of static things—substances with fixed properties. BITwiki follows a different approach based on process philosophy. Alfred North Whitehead's Process and Reality (1929) established that reality consists not of static substances but of "actual occasions"—momentary events of becoming. Knowledge is not a picture of fixed reality but a grasping of ongoing processes. This matters for BITwiki because: '' Knowledge artifacts are events, not objects '' Understanding emerges from ongoing engagement '' Revision is not correction but continuation '''Source''': Whitehead, A.N. (1929). ''Process and Reality''. Free Press. === Knowledge as Practice === Michel Foucault's Archaeology of Knowledge (1969) analyzed how knowledge is produced through specific practices. Knowledge is not discovered but constructed through historical discursive formations. Key insight: What counts as knowledge depends on the practices that produce it. Different practices produce different knowledges. There is no neutral view from nowhere. This informs BITwiki approach: '' All knowledge is situated in specific practices '' We document the practices, not just the results '' Multiple practices can produce valid but different knowledges '''Source''': Foucault, M. (1969). ''The Archaeology of Knowledge''. Routledge. === The Mangle of Practice === Andrew Pickering's The Mangle of Practice (1995) describes scientific practice as open-ended interplay between human and material agency. Knowledge emerges from the "dance of agency"—scientists propose, materials resist, scientists accommodate. This dynamic model replaces the static "scientific method" with ongoing tuning and adjustment. Knowledge is always provisional, always subject to further negotiation. BITwiki applies this by: '' Treating knowledge as ongoing process, not fixed product '' Expecting resistance and accommodation '' Building in mechanisms for continuous tuning '''Source''': Pickering, A. (1995). ''The Mangle of Practice''. University of Chicago Press. == Section IX: Epistemic Framework (v1.0.0 Framework) == === Context-Dependent Evidence === Evidence has no fixed value. What counts as good evidence depends on context. A peer-reviewed paper may be flawed by funding bias. An informal forum post may contain crucial technical detail. Blockchain data is valuable for blockchain analysis, irrelevant for biology. This follows from the research: '' Whitehead's prehension: grasping depends on the grasper '' Foucault's episteme: what counts as evidence varies by historical period '' Stengers' cosmopolitics: different actors have different evidentiary standards '''Source''': Stengers, I. (1996-1997). ''Cosmopolitics''. University of Minnesota Press. === Signal Fidelity === Claude Shannon's "A Mathematical Theory of Communication" (1948) established information theory. The signal-to-noise ratio measures meaningful information relative to interference. BITwiki applies this conceptually: '' Not all information is equally valuable '' Noise is context-dependent (what distracts in one context may inform in another) '' Quality is measured by signal fidelity, not volume '''Source''': Shannon, C.E. (1948). "A Mathematical Theory of Communication." ''Bell System Technical Journal''. Gregory Bateson extended this: "Information is a difference that makes a difference." Not all differences matter. The key is identifying which differences produce change in the receiving system. '''Source''': Bateson, G. (1972). ''Steps to an Ecology of Mind''. Chandler Publishing. === Autopoiesis and Self-Production === Maturana and Varela's Autopoiesis and Cognition (1980) defined living systems as self-producing. A living system produces its own components and maintains its own organization. BITwiki is designed as autopoietic: '' It produces its own knowledge components '' It maintains its own organizational structure '' It adapts through structural coupling with its environment '''Source''': Maturana, H.R. & Varela, F.J. (1980). ''Autopoiesis and Cognition''. D. Reidel. == Section X: The Three Documents Framework (v1.0.0) == === Charter: Values and Mission === The Charter establishes what BITwiki values and why it exists. It draws on: '' Axiology (study of values) as primary '' Hyper-realism: acknowledging constructed nature of knowledge '' Epistemic humility: openness to revision Values determine what we seek to know. They come first in the framework. === Constitution: Operations === The Constitution defines how BITwiki runs. It implements: '' Agent-centric authorship: AI agents execute human intent '' Context-dependent evidence: no fixed hierarchies '' Continuous refinement: knowledge as ongoing process Methods follow from values. How we know depends on what we value knowing. === Foundational Triad: Structure === The Triad explains the philosophical architecture: '' Axiology (values) first '' Epistemology (knowledge methods) second '' Ontology (what exists) third Structure emerges from values and methods. What we can represent depends on how we know and what we care about. == Section XI: Key Principles in Practice (v1.0.0) == === No Truth by Consensus === Agreement does not equal truth. Many sources can agree and still be wrong. This follows from: '' Foucault's analysis of power/knowledge '' Pickering's mangle: consensus can be stabilization of network, not truth '' Shannon's information theory: redundancy enables error correction but does not guarantee accuracy === Human Intent First === All knowledge starts with human values. AI agents execute that intent. This follows from: '' Whitehead's actual occasions: experience is primary '' Bateson's ecology of mind: cognition is systemic process '' Autopoiesis: systems self-produce based on their own organization === Continuous Refinement === Nothing is final.
